_note: What an author sends for review. The assessment tool and the risk tool WRITE it (Send for review); the report review tool READS it. It holds the text the client will receive, read back from the generated Word file, and the engagement behind it, so a reviewer can challenge a finding as well as its wording. A pack contains client data: handle it like the project file. Each tool carries its own copy of this contract; bump the schema string here when the shape changes, so that a mismatch fails loudly. Importers ACCEPT the listed schemas and reject unknown ones with a clear message.
_optional: Within spt-review-pack/1.0 these fields are OPTIONAL and additive, so a pack without them loads and shows exactly as before, and a reader that does not know them ignores them: engagement.fieldLabels, items[].targetId, items[].details, request, documents[].blocks[].runs[].c, and from and fileId on a reply in previousRound.comments[].replies. Nothing in request ever reaches Word or Excel.

shape.packId: unique id of this pack; a review file names the pack it answers
shape.reviewId: unique id of the review as a whole, the same on every round of one assessment
shape.round: 1, 2, 3...: goes up when the content or the round has moved on

engagement.scoringFamily: capability-sl, caf-achieved, domain-letter, program-maturity-ml, nis2-conformance, csms-conformance, risk-appetite-coherence; risk tool: risk-assessment
engagement.targetLabel: what one target is called: Zone, Site, Product...
engagement.fieldLabels: OPTIONAL. What this pack calls each item field, shown to the reviewer and the author in place of the assessment names: { answer, expected, evidence, notes, action, impact, priority, owner }, each a display label such as "Threat source", or null when the pack has no such field (its row is hidden and it is not offered for suggested wording or as a filter). A field left out, or the whole object absent, keeps the assessment label (Answer, Target, Evidence, Notes, Action, Business impact, Priority, Owner).

shape.request: OPTIONAL. The author's note to the reviewers, sent with this pack: { note: free text, neededBy: free text such as "Thursday 12 November" }. Present only when something was filled in; either part may be empty. Shown to the reviewer in the review tool; never in Word or Excel.

documents.title: the report's name, shown to the reviewer
documents.targetName: the target this document covers, or empty for a document covering all of them
documents.contentHash: hash of the client's text (App.DocxBlocks.contentHash), leaving out the cover and the document control fields that change on issue

runs.c: OPTIONAL. A 6-hex colour, only on a key swatch run (a lone shape such as a square in a chart colour), so the reviewer sees the key as printed

items.targetId: OPTIONAL. The authoring tool's own id for the target. A comment anchor that carries it is matched to the item by targetId when both have one, otherwise by targetName, so two targets with one name stay apart
items.title: requirement title
items.groupName: FR, principle, domain or category name
items.answer: the answer as a label: Partially achieved, SL 1, Not answered
items.expected: target or expected level, where the instrument has one
items.status: finding | met | recorded | to-assess | unanswered | na
items.shared: true when the answer comes from the system-wide layer rather than this target
items.details: OPTIONAL. Extra read-only rows shown after the standard ones: [[label, value], ...], for example [["Likelihood x impact", "Likely x Serious"], ["Affected FRs", "IAC, SI"]]. Not offered for suggested wording.

replies.from: OPTIONAL. "reviewer" on a reply a reviewer wrote (the replies of a review file); absent on the author's own
replies.fileId: OPTIONAL. On a reviewer's reply, the review file it came in

confirmedBy: names of reviewers who confirmed the fix

request.note: First round. The executive summary is new; the findings are as agreed on site.
